eligibility: Pearson describes techniques for manipulating formulas and solving problems, expanding the mathematical prerequisites of The Art of Computer Programming and providing over 500 exercises.
reason: The book's humor and history support mathematical training for computing; self-study is not an exemption.

eligibility: Halmos's preface, reproduced by Springer, explicitly aims to equip beginning advanced mathematics students with set-theoretic tools needed for groups, integrals and manifolds.
reason: It is foundational technical instruction, even though formalism is kept light.

eligibility: Pearson identifies Artin's Algebra as an honors undergraduate or beginning graduate course, with sequential chapters and exercises in matrices, groups and algebraic structures.
reason: Concrete motivation and integrated linear algebra remain part of a course textbook.

eligibility: Springer explicitly targets graduate students in axiomatic set theory and researchers, with technical development of forcing, ultrafilters, cardinal relations and independence results.
reason: Historical notes and a gentle introduction do not change its specialist training/reference purpose.

eligibility: Springer calls Axler's book a second-course textbook for undergraduate mathematics majors and graduates, with extensive exercises and an instructor solutions manual.
reason: Its determinant-free route is a pedagogical choice within technical linear-algebra instruction.

eligibility: The publisher's description reproduced in WorldCat identifies undergraduate abstract-algebra courses and future mathematics teachers as the audience, with themed exercises and systematic standard topics.
reason: Informal discussions replace a terse theorem style but still teach a technical curriculum.

eligibility: Princeton identifies this as Milnor's lecture-note exposition of Morse theory in Annals of Mathematics Studies, addressing the technical relation between functions, topology and manifold structure.
reason: It is a specialist mathematical method text; elegance and applications in physics do not make it a general history or narrative.

eligibility: Princeton's description identifies Real Analysis as volume three of a four-textbook analysis sequence, teaching measure theory, integration and Hilbert spaces.
reason: The individually nominated volume has the same explicit technical teaching purpose as the complete sequence.

eligibility: AMS states that Schultens's book grew from a graduate course and provides over 200 exercises, progressing from manifold definitions to normal surfaces, Heegaard splittings and curve complexes.
reason: The overview trains readers in low-dimensional topology; illustrations do not alter that role.

eligibility: The authors call the manuscript a bridge from an elementary PDE course to advanced textbooks. EMS contents develop elliptic estimates, nonlinear equations and obstacle problems.
reason: This is technical training in PDE regularity. The 2021 source referred to a prepublication manuscript; EMS confirms the final book published in 2022.

eligibility: Springer identifies Baldi's textbook for advanced undergraduates and graduates, with over 200 fully solved exercises, stochastic differential equations, simulation and finance applications.
reason: It develops technical stochastic-calculus skills and is explicitly suitable for courses or self-study.

eligibility: The authors' Cambridge preface develops Brownian paths through Hausdorff dimension, stochastic integrals and potential theory, with over 100 exercises across ten chapters.
reason: This is a specialist probability course and method text, not a popular account of random motion.

eligibility: Oxford describes systematic prerequisites in abstract and geometric measure theory followed by technical analysis of bounded variation, Mumford–Shah segmentation and free-discontinuity regularity.
reason: The book is a specialist research and training reference in variational analysis; engineering applications do not change the structure.

eligibility: Carter's own description says it covers a typical undergraduate group-theory course, including subgroups, homomorphisms, quotients, Sylow theory and Galois theory.
reason: The visual approach and low entry prerequisites are instructional features, not a different primary purpose.

eligibility: The source nominates Zakon's analysis series. The publisher-supplied volume descriptions and contents identify university lecture-note texts in rigorous analysis, set theory, real numbers, metric spaces and calculus.
reason: The nomination is a course-text series. No unsupported individual volumes are added beyond the nominated series scope.

eligibility: Cengage explicitly says Gallian's book is primarily for an abstract-algebra course whose purpose is computational ability and proof writing; it supplies over 1,750 exercises.
reason: Biographies, quotations and applications are teaching aids within that course structure.
